verdict_merge: PASS. Mergeable once (1) Mark's licence check L-tex is recorded (the merge waits on it by the plan's own pause point) and (2) the D-28 ordering is handled: whichever of PR #106 and PR #107 (fix/sky-mirror) merges second must replace the hand-copied frame map at physics/planets.gd:98 with SkyFrame.to_world64([v["x"], v["y"], v["z"]]) and re-run make golden + make capture-m5a; D-28's guard regex matches that line exactly, so an unfixed second merge turns make physics red, and worse, the body position and sun direction would keep the old det -1 map while body_basis (physics/planets.gd:126) follows the new one, mirroring the lit hemisphere and texture relative to the sky. The physics itself is right: the GDScript mirror is an operation-for-operation copy of celestial 0.1.0 reflect, 18 probe values hold at 1e-12, and on the GPU my own six-case check puts the terminator at exactly -R cos(alpha) and the integrated flux within 0.7% of discIlluminance for k = 1, 0.825 and 1.2 at 48, 60, 90 and 120 degrees. The 'almost fully lit' Earth on the contact sheet is the capture chain (clipped clouds + bloom + AgX), not the shader.

physics_gate_2.phases_and_terminator: RIGHT on the GPU. Evaluator-only golden (appended to tools/m5_golden.gd in the mutation copy, goldens' linear chain, 200 px disc, 1 deg fov): k 1.0 alpha 48: integrated / discIlluminance 1.0011, lit extent on the centre row 167.0 px (want 100 (1 + cos a) = 166.9), span -67..+100; k 0.825 alpha 48: 1.0013, 167.0; k 1.0 alpha 90: 0.9974, 100.0 (span +0..+100); k 0.825 alpha 90: 0.9986, 100.0; k 1.0 alpha 120: 0.9935, 50.0 (span +50..+100); k 1.2 alpha 60: 1.0004, 150.0. The terminator sits at exactly -R cos(alpha) and the phase law (lambertPhase / minnaertPhase) integrates on the GPU within 0.7%. On the production captures (AgX + glow) the row measurement gives Mercury 70 deg 0.666-0.689 of D (want 0.671), Moon 90 deg 0.44-0.47 (want 0.50; the AgX toe eats the last ~5 px of the cos i ramp), Venus 60 deg 0.78-0.80 (want 0.75; bloom), Earth 48 deg 0.89-0.90 (want 0.833; clipped clouds bloom ~10 px past the terminator at -65 px). So the contact-sheet impression that Earth is almost fully lit is the capture chain, not the lighting.
physics_gate_2.terminator_toward_sun: For all nine captures the Sun projects at camera x > 0 and the lit centroid is on the right; Earth's sun_dir has camera y -0.09, so its terminator is slightly tilted, as it should be with the sub-solar latitude at -15 deg.
physics_gate_2.pole_up: For all nine captures the pole projects at screen x 0.000 and y +0.93 to +1.00 (Uranus +0.47 because its pole points near the Sun, pole.sun +0.88); Jupiter's and Saturn's bands are horizontal, Mars's north cap is at the top.
physics_gate_2.minnaert_lambert: physics/planets.gd is an operation-for-operation mirror of celestial 0.1.0 reflect (starIlluminanceAt, lambertPhase with the p < 0 clamp, lambertRadiance, minnaertRadiance with the four branches, rhoFromGeometricAlbedo, lonIntegral as composite Simpson 256 with the same weights and order, minnaertPhase, phaseFunction, discIlluminance): 18 probe values at 1e-12. The shader mirrors it, including the package-advised cos e >= 1e-3 clamp for k < 1. The only photometric maths that exists without a package copy is the solar limb-darkening normalisation (gate 3, see fidelity).
physics_gate_2.sun_limb_darkening: sun_disc.png (0.05 AU, 72 px, EV fixed for the centre at linear 0.25): linear luminance centre 0.2474, L/L0 0.936 / 0.777 / 0.697 / 0.622 / 0.575 at r = 0.5 / 0.8 / 0.9 / 0.95 / 0.98 (model 0.920 / 0.760 / 0.662 / 0.587 / 0.519; the capture's AgX and glow raise the limb a few percent). Monotonic darkening to the limb is there; the CPU normalisation is tested (_limb_mean) but the shader's is not (mutation H survived).
physics_gate_2.point_disc_handoff: Seamless: G-M5-6 1.9 px point 1.0010 vs 2.1 px disc 1.0013; the CPU half (test_planets) 1.00001 at both; crossover_pair.png shows the PSF blob and the 2-px disc at equal integrated brightness; the point MultiMesh shares the star quad and uniforms so aberration, Doppler and PSF are the stars'.
physics_gate_2.near_field_claim: Verified in substance, coefficient corrected: for a Lambert sphere at opposition at finite distance (sunlight parallel), my exact integral exceeds the far-field pi (R/d)^2 form by +0.25% at R/d 0.0032 (G-M5-4 measured +0.21%), +0.6% at R/d 0.00785 (0.9 deg), +3.7% at 0.05, +7.3% at 0.1, +18.1% at 0.26 (a 30 deg globe). First order is about 0.75 R/d, not the 1.5 R/d written at tools/m5_golden.gd:94-97. The drawn radiance is the exact one; the sim's e_v_lux is far-field; M5.4's meter reads the drawn image, so the discrepancy only matters when it meters a globe wider than ~5 deg, and it is the far-field number that is approximate.
physics_gate_2.precision_gate_5: No raw km in a Vector3: Planets.place / world_of / length64 are float64 and only the O(PLACE) results become float32 (test_placement_precision: 4 cases, angular radius to 1e-6, centre at PLACE to 1e-5); point sources are placed in float64 ly along the direction with the flux rescaled by POINT_LY^2 / |p|^2. Lookup table data/planets/ALBEDO: 9 means in (0, 1], checked against the sim's k and the pins; the independent --check (ray-sampled disc at 12 longitudes) agrees within 0.04%.
physics_gate_2.sky_mirror_D28: Today every planet direction, sun direction and pole goes through the same det -1 map, so the lit side, the texture and the sky are mutually consistent (the mirror is the sky's bug, not this PR's). planets/system_view.gd does NOT use the shared Starfield.galactic_to_world for positions: Planets.world_of (physics/planets.gd:97-98) is a float64 hand copy, used at planets/system_view.gd:96, 119, 124, 165 and tools/m5_golden.gd:270; Planets.body_basis (physics/planets.gd:126) does use the shared map. With D-28 the shared map changes to det +1 and the hand copy does not: the body and its sun direction would stay mirrored while its pole/texture frame flips. Required follow-up for whichever PR merges second: physics/planets.gd:98 -> SkyFrame.to_world64([v["x"], v["y"], v["z"]]), then make test golden capture-m5a and re-open the renders. The existing test 'sun_dir galactic -x -> world +Z' remains valid under either map.

findings.issue: world_of() is a float64 hand copy of the galactic -> world axis map (y, z, -x); body_basis() at :126 uses the shared Starfield.galactic_to_world. D-28 (PR #107, fix/sky-mirror) changes the shared map to (-y, z, -x), det +1, adds SkyFrame.to_world64 and a guard whose pattern (\w+)\["y"\],\s*\1\["z"\],\s*-\1\["x"\] matches this line.
findings.suggestion: Whichever of #106 and #107 merges second: return SkyFrame.to_world64([v["x"], v["y"], v["z"]]); then make test golden capture-m5a and re-open the renders (the lit side will swap to the left, which is the real sky).

findings.issue: make golden-m5 never times out: with a parse error in tools/m5_golden.gd load() returns null, .new() errors inside _ready, and Godot sits with no output until killed (reproduced, 90 s alarm). _run_golden shares the pattern.

findings.issue: Near-field comment says 'about 1.5 R/d: +1.2% at 0.9 deg'; the exact finite-distance integral is about 0.75 R/d to first order (+0.6% at 0.9 deg, +0.25% at the golden's 0.37 deg where 1.0021 was measured). The +19% at 30 deg figure is right (+18.1% exact).
findings.suggestion: Correct the coefficient; keep the M5.4 note (the meter sees the exact drawn radiance; e_v_lux is far-field).

findings.issue: The reference-render EV assumes textures reach ~2x their mean; Earth's clouds reach ~6x (mean 0.1597 with white clouds), so earth_phase48.png clips the clouds and the glow crosses the terminator by ~10 px; the contact sheet reads as almost fully lit although the shader puts the terminator at -R cos(48.2 deg) exactly.
findings.suggestion: Store each texture's max (or 99th percentile) in ALBEDO and expose for it, or disable glow in the capture environment; re-capture.

findings.issue: Gate 3: the solar limb-darkening law (L0 = mean / (1 - u/3), L = L0 (1 - u (1 - mu))) exists only in GDScript and the shader; celestial 0.1.0 has no star-disc model.
findings.suggestion: Add limbDarkenedRadiance(mean, mu, u) to sunholo/celestial (0.1.1, with the disc-mean test) and cite it from the mirror.

findings.issue: _find_e1 leaves e1_au at its previous value when a section has neither a visible star nor a lit body (stale across systems; harmless with Sol only).
findings.suggestion: Reset to 0 at the top of update() or carry e1 in the protocol (M5.1 follow-up).
